claim: Pancreatic cancer (PC) is one of the most lethal tumors with a poor prognosis, and patients show one of the lowest 5-year overall survival rates of all cancer patients, with approximately 13%.
source: Pancreatic cancer (PC) is one of the most lethal tumors having a poor prognosis, and patients suffering from this disease show one of the lowest 5-year overall survival rates of all cancer patients, with approximately 13%.
evidence: This claim cites a specific survival statistic (13%) that represents established knowledge in oncology literature, though no direct citation is provided in this sentence.

claim: One of the main reasons for the poor prognosis of pancreatic cancer is the lack of proper early detection possibility, resulting in late diagnosis often in advanced, metastatic stage.
source: One of the main reasons for this dismissal prognosis is the lack of a proper early detection possibility, resulting in late diagnosing often in advanced, metastatic stage (Bamankar and Londhe, 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Bamankar and Londhe, 2023.

claim: Approximately 90% of pancreatic cancers are classified as pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC).
source: The detection and diagnosis of PC, of which approximately 90% are classified as pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), currently relies primarily on modalities of medical imaging, such as computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance imaging, positron emission tomography, and transabdominal ultrasonography (Wang et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Wang et al., 2021, which provides the classification statistic.

claim: The detection and diagnosis of PC currently relies primarily on modalities of medical imaging, such as computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance imaging, positron emission tomography, and transabdominal ultrasonography.
source: The detection and diagnosis of PC, of which approximately 90% are classified as pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), currently relies primarily on modalities of medical imaging, such as computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance imaging, positron emission tomography, and transabdominal ultrasonography (Wang et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Wang et al., 2021.

claim: The most common biomarker considered for PDAC differential diagnosis is elevated blood abundance of carbohydrate antigen 19-9 (CA19-9) and carcinoembryonic antigen.
source: The most common biomarker considered for PDAC differential diagnosis is elevated blood abundancy of carbohydrate antigen 19-9 (CA19-9) and carcinoembryonic antigen, though these are only used as prognostic markers and not effective for screening or early diagnosis (Bestari et al., 2024).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Bestari et al., 2024.

claim: CA19-9 and carcinoembryonic antigen are only used as prognostic markers and not effective for screening or early diagnosis of PDAC.
source: The most common biomarker considered for PDAC differential diagnosis is elevated blood abundancy of carbohydrate antigen 19-9 (CA19-9) and carcinoembryonic antigen, though these are only used as prognostic markers and not effective for screening or early diagnosis (Bestari et al., 2024).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Bestari et al., 2024.

claim: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are non-coding RNAs that target genes and regulate their expression by inhibiting mRNA translation or enhancing their degradation.
source: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are non-coding RNAs that target genes and regulate their expression by inhibiting mRNA translation or enhancing their degradation (Rashid et al., 2024).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Rashid et al., 2024.

claim: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) carry the material of their secreting cells and are considered to contain tumor-derived elements, showcasing their molecular fingerprint.
source: Currently, extracellular vesicles (EVs) are gaining attention as disease-specific markers since they carry the material of their secreting cells and are therefore considered to contain tumor-derived elements, showcasing their molecular fingerprint (Bamankar and Londhe, 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Bamankar and Londhe, 2023.

claim: miRNA derived from small EVs play a role in differentiation and metastasis of cancer.
source: It has been shown multiple times that miRNA derived from small EVs play a role in differentiation and metastasis of cancer (Mok et al., 2024; Min et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Mok et al., 2024 and Min et al., 2019.

claim: Numerous miRNAs have been described using co-expression network analysis that might be applied as diagnostic or prognostic biomarker, for patient stratification or disease recurrence.
source: Numerous miRNAs have been described using co-expression network analysis that might be applied as diagnostic or prognostic biomarker, for patient stratification or disease recurrence (Tiwari et al., 2024).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Tiwari et al., 2024.

claim: A three-serum miRNA signature was developed using machine-learning algorithms that effectively provides early warning of premalignant PC.
source: For example, we used machine-learning algorithms to assist in the development of a three-serum miRNA signature that effectively provides early warning of premalignant PC (Shi et al., 2024).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Shi et al., 2024, which describes the authors' previous work.

claim: A model based on machine-learning algorithms focuses on the immune subtypes of triple-negative breast cancer, offering critical insights for identifying patients who may benefit from immunotherapy.
source: Another model, based on machine-learning algorithms, focuses on the immune subtypes of triple-negative breast cancer, offering critical insights for identifying patients who may benefit from immunotherapy (Chen et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Chen et al., 2021.

claim: Radiogenomics technology integrates the quantification of image features from CT or magnetic resonance imaging, which are then correlated with genomic signatures and allows for a non-invasive prediction of molecular characteristics.
source: This novel approach integrates the quantification of image features from CT or magnetic resonance imaging, which are then correlated with genomic signatures and allows for a non-invasive prediction of molecular characteristics (Casà et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Casà et al., 2022.

claim: Radiogenomic analysis can predict the occurrence of p53 mutations using CT images and hence make a statement on the prognosis.
source: Such as, claim to be able to predict the occurrence of p53 mutations using CT images by radiogenomic analysis and hence make a statement on the prognosis (Iwatate et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Iwatate et al., 2020.

claim: A total of 272 patients enrolled in this study providing CT imaging, including 173 in UMMD and JHC center while 99 in WUH center.
source: A total of 272 patients enrolled in this study providing CT imaging, including 173 in UMMD and JHC center while 99 in WUH center.
evidence: This claim presents data from the study's patient enrollment.

claim: In the UMMD and JHC center, 46 pancreatic benign lesion and 127 PC CT images were included.
source: In the UMMD and JHC center, also including 46 pancreatic benign lesion and 127 PC CT images.
evidence: This claim presents data from the study's patient enrollment.

claim: Most pancreatic patients in UMMD and JHC center are older with obesity, but less smoking or alcohol and less with diabetes.
source: Most pancreatic patients in this center are older with obesity, but less smoking or alcohol and less with diabetes.
evidence: This claim presents demographic data from the study cohort.

claim: For the WUH center, most PC patients are female and also have a high incidence of older age and obesity.
source: For the WUH center, most PC patients are female and also have a high incidence of older age and obesity.
evidence: This claim presents demographic data from the study cohort.

claim: About 82.5% (52/63) patients in the DUH cohort are older, and 34 patients are female.
source: About 82.5% (52/63) patients are older, and 34 patients are female.
evidence: This claim presents demographic data from the study cohort.

claim: After propensity score matching (PSM), both center baseline differences were removed.
source: After the match, we found both center baseline differences were removed (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by data analysis results shown in Figure 2A.

claim: A total of n = 88 significant features demonstrate differences between benign lesions and aggressive tumors.
source: Then the difference expression radiomics features was conducted, the results indicate that a total of n = 88 significant features demonstrate differences between groups (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by radiomics analysis results shown in Figure 2B.

claim: A total of 12 features were identified as important features by Boruta algorithms.
source: We use Boruta algorithms to select the important features, and the results show that a total of 12 features were identified (Figure 2—source data 1), which is more than shadow features.
evidence: This claim is supported by feature selection analysis using Boruta algorithms.

claim: Four features were selected as key features by Lasso regression (LR) algorithms.
source: In addition, after inputting the above features into Lasso regression (LR) algorithms, we found that four features are listed as key features (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by LASSO regression analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The four radiomics feature-related signature shows high accuracy in predicting PDAC manifestation in the WUH test dataset with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.911.
source: Based on the LR model with regression coefficient and feature expression, we build a four radiomics feature-related signature and validate the prediction ability in WUH center data, revealing a signature accuracy of prediction efficiency (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.911) (Figure 2E, F).
evidence: This claim is supported by validation results shown in Figure 2E and 2F.

claim: The green module was identified as the key module by WGCNA analysis and includes 12 hub co-expressed miRNAs.
source: According to the WGCNA analysis, the green module was identified as the key module and includes 12 hub co-expressed miRNAs.
evidence: This claim is supported by WGCNA analysis results.

claim: The number of low-abundance miRNAs calculated was n = 295.
source: The number of low-abundance miRNAs calculated was n = 295.
evidence: This claim presents data from miRNA abundance analysis.

claim: Three miRNAs (hsa-miR-1260b, hsa-miR-151a-3p, and hsa-miR-5695) were identified by merging WGCNA results and low-abundance miRNAs.
source: Merging both results, three miRNAs are identified (hsa-miR-1260b, hsa-miR-151a-3p, and hsa-miR-5695) and selected for subsequent alignment with associated radiomic features (Figure 3A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by analysis results shown in Figure 3A-C.

claim: The three key miRNAs (hsa-miR-1260b, hsa-miR-151a-3p, and hsa-miR-5695) show significantly different expression levels in tumor conditions compared to healthy samples in serum.
source: We use serum and tissue samples to validate the expression of three hub EV miRNAs, and the results show that compared with healthy serum samples, these three miRNAs are enriched in tumor patient serum samples.
evidence: This claim is supported by validation experiments comparing tumor and healthy serum samples.

claim: The three key miRNAs show upregulation in tumor tissue compared to non-tumor tissue.
source: Interestingly, this correlation of upregulation in tumor conditions was also true when comparing tumor tissue with non-tumor tissue (Figure 3D–I).
evidence: This claim is supported by tissue validation results shown in Figure 3D-I.

claim: In the GBM-default (cut-off = 0.75) model, three EV miRNAs show high accuracy to predict PC with training accuracy of 0.978 and AUC = 0.978.
source: The results show that in the GBM-default (cut-off = 0.75) model, three EV miRNAs show a high accuracy to predict the PC with the training accuracy of 0.978 with AUC = 0.978, and two test dataset accuracies are 0.923 with AUC = 0.919, and 0.871 with AUC = 0.857, respectively.
evidence: This claim is supported by machine learning model performance data.

claim: The three EV miRNAs achieved test dataset accuracies of 0.923 with AUC = 0.919, and 0.871 with AUC = 0.857 in two independent test datasets.
source: The results show that in the GBM-default (cut-off = 0.75) model, three EV miRNAs show a high accuracy to predict the PC with the training accuracy of 0.978 with AUC = 0.978, and two test dataset accuracies are 0.923 with AUC = 0.919, and 0.871 with AUC = 0.857, respectively.
evidence: This claim is supported by machine learning model performance data on test datasets.

claim: The extended dataset validation via GBM shows high diagnostic accuracy of the three EV miRNAs with accuracy = 0.894 and AUC = 0.897.
source: The results of the extended dataset validation via GBM further highlight the high diagnostic accuracy of the three EV miRNAs (accuracy = 0.894, and AUC = 0.897) (Figure 4), while the CA19-9 predict AUC is 0.843 (95% CI, 0.762–0.924).
evidence: This claim is supported by extended validation results shown in Figure 4.

claim: The CA19-9 predict AUC is 0.843 (95% CI, 0.762–0.924).
source: The results of the extended dataset validation via GBM further highlight the high diagnostic accuracy of the three EV miRNAs (accuracy = 0.894, and AUC = 0.897) (Figure 4), while the CA19-9 predict AUC is 0.843 (95% CI, 0.762–0.924).
evidence: This claim is supported by comparative analysis with the standard biomarker CA19-9.

claim: A total of 117 mRNA shared candidate targets were obtained after predicting molecular targets of three miRNAs.
source: After predicting molecular targets of three miRNAs, we obtain a number of 117 mRNA shared candidate targets (Figure 5—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by target prediction analysis.

claim: Tumors can be stratified into two subtypes termed Cluster 1 (C1) and C2 based on the expression level of the 117 mRNA targets.
source: Stratifying the tumors according to the level of expression of those allows the differentiation of tumors in the cluster into two subtypes termed Cluster 1 (C1) and C2 (Figure 5—source data 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by clustering analysis results.

claim: C2 patients feature prolonged survival outcome compared with C1, in both overall survival time (OS) and disease free survival time (DFS).
source: The survival analysis shows that compared with C1, the C2 patients feature a prolonged survival outcome, no matter in overall survival time (OS) or disease free survival time (DFS) (Figure 5B, C).
evidence: This claim is supported by survival analysis results shown in Figure 5B and 5C.

claim: C1 subtype patients are older in age and carry bigger tumor sizes and higher number of tumor cell positive lymph nodes compared with C2 subtype patients.
source: In addition, analyzing the relationship with clinical factors of patients, we also found the C1 subtype patients are older in age and carry bigger tumor sizes and higher number of tumor cell positive lymph nodes (Figure 5D–F), when compared with C2 subtype patients.
evidence: This claim is supported by clinical correlation analysis shown in Figure 5D-F.

claim: C1 patients are particularly aggressive in female patients, featuring a high number of tumors containing perineural invasion (PNI) and advanced pathological tumor staging.
source: We also demonstrate C1 patients are particularly aggressive in female patients, featuring a high number of tumors containing perineural invasion (PNI) and advanced pathological tumor staging (Figure 5G–I).
evidence: This claim is supported by clinical correlation analysis shown in Figure 5G-I.

claim: C2 tumors are significantly more enriched for immune cell signals, including those for CD8 T cells, cytotoxic lymphocytes, and NK cells.
source: Testing for gene signatures that indicate immune cell existence, we show that C2 tumors are significantly more enriched for immune cell signals, including those for CD8 T cells, cytotoxic lymphocytes, and NK cells (Figure 6A, B).
evidence: This claim is supported by immune cell infiltration analysis shown in Figure 6A and 6B.

claim: C2 subtype samples show a more physiological expression signature in terms of immune checkpoints as compared to C1 tumors.
source: In addition, samples of patients of that subtype also show a more physiological expression signature in terms of immune checkpoints as compared to C1 tumors (Figure 6C).
evidence: This claim is supported by immune checkpoint expression analysis shown in Figure 6C.

claim: C1 patients might be more sensitive to AKT INHIBITOR VIII, Bleomycin, Dasatinib, GNF-2, PF-562271, Refametinib, and BMS-509744 compared to C2 subtypes.
source: We use Genomics of Drug Sensitivity in Cancer (GDSC) data to merge cell line response data and expression data with expression signals in C1 and C2 tumors. This analysis indicated that C1 patients may benefit from therapy with FDA-approved AKT inhibitor VIII, Bleomycin, Dasatinib, GNF-2, PF-562271, Refametinib, and BMS-509744 (Figure 6D).
evidence: This claim is supported by drug sensitivity prediction analysis using GDSC data, shown in Figure 6D.

claim: The C1 subtype is enriched for intermediate filament organization, GOCC ribosome, as well as GOMF symporter activity.
source: GO functional enrichment analysis indicated that the C1 subtype is enriched for intermediate filament organization, GOCC ribosome, as well as GOMF symporter activity (Figure 7A, B).
evidence: This claim is supported by GO functional enrichment analysis shown in Figure 7A and 7B.

claim: The C1 subtype was activated with the Reactome fatty acids, Reactome diseases of metabolism, as well as Reactome biological oxidations pathways.
source: Pathway enrichment analysis showed that the C1 subtype was activated with the Reactome fatty acids, Reactome diseases of metabolism, as well as Reactome biological oxidations pathways, and may be inhibited with Reactome apoptosis, Reactome DNA repair, and Reactome signaling by Hippo pathways (Figure 7C).
evidence: This claim is supported by pathway enrichment analysis shown in Figure 7C.

claim: The C1 subtype may be inhibited with Reactome apoptosis, Reactome DNA repair, and Reactome signaling by Hippo pathways.
source: Pathway enrichment analysis showed that the C1 subtype was activated with the Reactome fatty acids, Reactome diseases of metabolism, as well as Reactome biological oxidations pathways, and may be inhibited with Reactome apoptosis, Reactome DNA repair, and Reactome signaling by Hippo pathways (Figure 7C).
evidence: This claim is supported by pathway enrichment analysis shown in Figure 7C.

claim: This study is the first to distinguish between benign lesions and PC by identifying novel and significant plasma EV microRNAs based on differential radiomics features.
source: This study is the first to distinguish between benign lesions and PC by identifying novel and significant plasma EV microRNAs based on differential radiomics features.
evidence: This claim asserts a novel contribution of the study based on the authors' assessment of the literature.

claim: Low-abundance microRNAs are often overlooked in routine RNA sequencing analyses.
source: We focused on low-abundance microRNAs, which are often overlooked in routine RNA sequencing analyses.
evidence: This claim is based on general knowledge about RNA sequencing practices.

claim: PC remains one of the most lethal diseases, with insufficient early detection methods and limited treatment options.
source: PC remains one of the most lethal diseases, with insufficient early detection methods and limited treatment options (Halbrook et al., 2023; Fahrmann et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Halbrook et al., 2023 and Fahrmann et al., 2021.

claim: Highly abundant microRNAs often mask the signals of many others that are present at very low abundance during routine analysis.
source: Although numerous studies have reported on microRNA sequencing results (Yang et al., 2021), highly abundant microRNAs often mask the signals of many others that are present at very low abundance during routine analysis.
evidence: This claim is based on general knowledge about RNA sequencing and signal detection, with a citation to Yang et al., 2021 for context.

claim: If a microRNA is associated with tumor development, it is likely to be in low abundance during early detection and may even be undetectable in benign lesions.
source: Furthermore, if a microRNA is associated with tumor development, it is likely to be in low abundance during early detection and may even be undetectable in benign lesions.
evidence: This claim is based on logical inference about tumor-associated biomarkers.

claim: hsa-miR-1260b and hsa-miR-5695 were undetectable in PC samples.
source: These microRNAs showed significantly higher expression in PC blood than in non-malignant cancer patients' plasma, with hsa-miR-1260b and hsa-miR-5695 undetectable in PC samples.
evidence: This claim presents data from the study's expression analysis.

claim: The model based on three microRNAs demonstrated strong performance in the training group with AUC of 0.978, sensitivity of 0.97, and specificity of 0.99.
source: The model based on these three microRNAs demonstrated strong performance in the training group (AUC, 0.978; sensitivity, 0.97; specificity, 0.99), testing group (AUC, 0.919; sensitivity, 0.96; specificity, 0.88), and external testing group (AUC, 0.897; sensitivity, 0.90; specificity, 0.89).

claim: The model based on three microRNAs demonstrated strong performance in the testing group with AUC of 0.919, sensitivity of 0.96, and specificity of 0.88.
source: The model based on these three microRNAs demonstrated strong performance in the training group (AUC, 0.978; sensitivity, 0.97; specificity, 0.99), testing group (AUC, 0.919; sensitivity, 0.96; specificity, 0.88), and external testing group (AUC, 0.897; sensitivity, 0.90; specificity, 0.89).
evidence: This claim presents performance metrics from the study's diagnostic model.

claim: The model based on three microRNAs demonstrated strong performance in the external testing group with AUC of 0.897, sensitivity of 0.90, and specificity of 0.89.
source: The model based on these three microRNAs demonstrated strong performance in the training group (AUC, 0.978; sensitivity, 0.97; specificity, 0.99), testing group (AUC, 0.919; sensitivity, 0.96; specificity, 0.88), and external testing group (AUC, 0.897; sensitivity, 0.90; specificity, 0.89).
evidence: This claim presents performance metrics from the study's diagnostic model.

claim: Previous studies on microRNAs as diagnostic biomarkers for PC vs healthy controls report AUCs of 0.78–0.96 and sensitivities of 0.62–0.88.
source: Previous studies on microRNAs as diagnostic biomarkers for PC vs healthy controls report AUCs of 0.78–0.96 and sensitivities of 0.62–0.88 (Yang et al., 2021), but many lack external validation (Liu et al., 2012; Wang, 2020).

source: Previous studies on microRNAs as diagnostic biomarkers for PC vs healthy controls report AUCs of 0.78–0.96 and sensitivities of 0.62–0.88 (Yang et al., 2021), but many lack external validation (Liu et al., 2012; Wang, 2020).

claim: One case–control study identified two diagnostic panels based on microRNA expression: index I with 4 microRNAs (AUC, 0.86; sensitivity, 0.85; specificity, 0.64) and index II with 10 microRNAs (AUC, 0.93; sensitivity, 0.85; specificity, 0.85).
source: One case–control study identified two diagnostic panels based on microRNA expression (index I: 4 microRNAs; AUC, 0.86; sensitivity, 0.85; specificity, 0.64; index II: 10 microRNAs; AUC, 0.93; sensitivity, 0.85; specificity, 0.85) (Schultz et al., 2014).

claim: None of the three identified microRNAs (hsa-miR-1260b, hsa-miR-151a-3p, hsa-miR-5695) have been reported in the context of diagnostic biomarkers in PC.

claim: hsa-miR-5695 has only indirectly been linked to breast carcinogenesis and subtypes of metastatic prostate cancer.
source: Moreover, to our knowledge, hsa-miR-5695 has only indirectly been linked to breast carcinogenesis (Søkilde et al., 2019) and subtypes of metastatic prostate cancer (Watahiki et al., 2011), while hsa-miR-1260b has been implicated in promoting tumorigenesis in lung cancer (Kim et al., 2021), breast cancer (Park et al., 2022), sarcoma (Morita et al., 2020), and prostate cancer (Hirata et al., 2014).

evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Kim et al., 2021, Park et al., 2022, Morita et al., 2020, and Hirata et al., 2014.

claim: hsa-miR-1260b was identified as one of the top upregulated signals in plasma of IPMN cases compared to non-diseased controls.

claim: Exosomal hsa-miR-151a-3p has emerged as a potential novel biomarker for predicting bone metastasis in lung cancer.
source: Exosomal hsa-miR-151a-3p has emerged as a potential novel biomarker for predicting bone metastasis in lung cancer (Zhao et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Zhao et al., 2023.

claim: Circulating 2′-O-methylated form of hsa-miR-151a-3p is upregulated in total fraction of plasma of PDAC patients compared to those derived from healthy donors or patients with chronic pancreatitis.
source: A very recent report of results of a multicenter trial in Asian participants also identified circulating 2′-O-methylated form of hsa-miR-151a-3p is upregulated in total fraction of plasma of PDAC patients compared to those derived from healthy donors or patients with chronic pancreatitis (Yang et al., 2024).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Yang et al., 2024.

claim: PC currently has only two standard systemic treatments with limited efficacy.
source: PC currently has only two standard systemic treatments with limited efficacy, and the patient population responsive to immunotherapy and targeted therapy remains unclear (Neoptolemos et al., 2018).

source: Patients classified as C2 had better prognoses, with higher immune cell infiltration and more immune checkpoint expression, suggesting they may be suitable for immunotherapy after standard treatment.

evidence: This claim combines data analysis results with inference about pathway activity.

claim: Using the MCP-counter algorithm for blood samples is a limitation of the study, as it was originally designed for solid tissues, which may affect the accuracy of cell population quantification in the blood.
source: Additionally, using the Microenvironment Cell Populations-counter (MCP-counter) algorithm for blood samples is a limitation of our study, as it was originally designed for solid tissues, which may affect the accuracy of cell population quantification in the blood.

claim: The EV purification did not use measures to enrich for cancer cell-derived EVs such as CD147 membrane presenting amplitude.
source: Lastly, since our EV purification did not use measures to enrich for cancer cell-derived EVs such as CD147 membrane presenting amplitude (Ko et al., 2023), we cannot exclude contamination of our miRNA data due to signals from non-cancer cell background, which might impact the cancer specificity of our proposed blood test.
evidence: This claim acknowledges a methodological limitation with a citation to Ko et al., 2023.

claim: Contamination of miRNA data due to signals from non-cancer cell background cannot be excluded, which might impact the cancer specificity of the proposed blood test.
source: Lastly, since our EV purification did not use measures to enrich for cancer cell-derived EVs such as CD147 membrane presenting amplitude (Ko et al., 2023), we cannot exclude contamination of our miRNA data due to signals from non-cancer cell background, which might impact the cancer specificity of our proposed blood test.

claim: All CT images were acquired using a 64-slice multidetector spiral CT scanner, with a standard slice thickness of 1.0–1.5 mm and a reconstruction interval of 1 mm.
source: All CT images were acquired using a 64-slice multidetector spiral CT scanner, with a standard slice thickness of 1.0–1.5 mm and a reconstruction interval of 1 mm.

evidence: This claim describes the methodological choice for image selection based on imaging characteristics.

source: To ensure data consistency, all imaging data underwent preprocessing, including resampling, intensity normalization of grayscale values, and N4 bias field correction to address potential low-frequency signal inhomogeneities.
evidence: This claim describes the preprocessing steps applied to the imaging data.

claim: Low-abundance miRNAs are defined as the EV miRNAs with the lowest 30% Counts Per Million (CPM) value across all samples.
source: Low-abundance miRNAs are defined as the EV miRNAs with the lowest 30% Counts Per Million (CPM) value across all samples.
evidence: This claim defines the operational definition used in the study for low-abundance miRNAs.

claim: The soft-thresholding power of WGCNA was automatically defined by the model.
source: The soft-thresholding power of WGCNA was automatically defined by the model, which was then assisting in calculating the expression correlation with (1) a given miRNA to obtain gene significance (GS) and (2) of module membership (MM) with miRNAs to obtain MM.
evidence: This claim describes the methodological approach for WGCNA analysis.

claim: Based on the cut-off criteria (|MM| >0.5 and |GS| >0.1), significant miRNAs related to low- and high-risk images were obtained.
source: Based on the cut-off criteria (|MM| >0.5 and |GS| >0.1), we obtain the significant miRNAs related to low- and high-risk images, respectively.
evidence: This claim describes the cut-off criteria used for identifying significant miRNAs in WGCNA.

claim: Ten machine-learning algorithms (GBM, KNN, Lasso, XGBoost, ENR, SVM, LR, RR, StepWise, and QDA) were used to select the best model for prediction.
source: Then we use ten machine-learning algorithms (Gradient Boosting Machine [GBM], KNN, Lasso, XGBoost, ENR, SVM, LR, RR, StepWise, and QDA) composition to select the best model for prediction.
evidence: This claim describes the machine learning approach used in the study.

claim: The miRPathDB v2.0 database was used to predict the candidate target mRNAs of hub EV miRNAs.
source: To discover the candidate regulation mechanisms of hub EV miRNAs, we use miRPathDB v2.0 database (https://mpd.bioinf.uni-sb.de/overview.html) to predict the candidate target mRNAs of hub EV miRNAs.
evidence: This claim describes the database used for target prediction.

claim: The R package ConsensusClusterPlus was used to perform the cluster analysis of common target mRNAs.
source: We use the R package ConsensusClusterPlus to perform the cluster analysis of common target mRNAs and rank the best cluster results according to the Consensus value output received.
evidence: This claim describes the clustering method used in the study.

claim: The MCP-counter algorithms were used to calculate immune cell infiltration of each sample.
source: We use the MCP-counter algorithms to calculate immune cell infiltration of each sample and calculate the difference in the two tumor subtypes for each immune cell type separately.
